config.title: Sick Leave in Berlin - FAQ
config.subtitle: How long full pay lasts, when the six weeks start again, what Krankengeld pays and how to get a certificate in Berlin when your practice is full.

items.q: How many days can I be sick in Berlin before I need a doctor's note?
items.a: Under the Entgeltfortzahlungsgesetz the certificate is due once the incapacity lasts longer than three calendar days, and then at the latest on the next working day. Your employer is allowed to demand it earlier, including from the first day, and many employment contracts in Berlin do exactly that. Telling your employer that you are ill is a separate duty and it applies from the first morning, before your shift starts.

items.q: Do I get six weeks of full pay every time I am ill?
items.a: Only for a new illness. For one and the same illness a fresh six weeks opens only if you were free of that illness for at least six months before the new incapacity, or if twelve months have passed since the first day you were off with it. Between those dates every day off with that illness comes out of the same 42 calendar days. A different diagnosis has its own 42 days once the first entitlement is finished.

Krankengeld is 70 percent of your gross pay, capped at 90 percent of your net, and capped again by the contribution ceiling of 5,812.50 euros a month. That gives a maximum of 135.63 euros a day, or 4,068.90 euros for a 30-day month before deductions. Your own share of pension, unemployment and long-term care contributions comes off that, roughly 12.4 percent, so the highest amount that actually lands is around 3,560 euros a month. No health insurance contribution is charged on Krankengeld.

For one and the same illness it runs for at most 78 weeks within any three years, counted from the day the incapacity began, and the six weeks of continued pay from your employer count towards that total. An additional illness arriving during the run does not extend it. A new three-year period only opens a new claim if you were free of that illness for six months and were working or available for work in the meantime.

items.q: Can I get a sick note by telephone in Germany?
items.a: Yes, for up to five calendar days, as long as the practice already knows you from an earlier treatment, the illness has no severe symptoms and a video consultation is not the better route. A follow-up certificate by telephone only works when the first one was issued in person. The coalition agreed in July 2026 to abolish the telephone route and to require a certificate from the first day, but no law had been passed when this page was last checked, so the current rules still apply.

items.q: Where can I get a sick note in Berlin at the weekend?
items.a: Call 116117, the patient service of the Kassenarztliche Vereinigung Berlin. It is free for everyone in statutory insurance, it runs round the clock, and it covers both the Arztlicher Bereitschaftsdienst and the appointment service. The Bereitschaftspraxen reached through that number can issue a certificate, and a doctor may establish incapacity on any calendar day, Sundays and public holidays included.

items.q: How many days can I take off for a sick child in 2026?
items.a: In calendar year 2026 the entitlement is 15 working days per child per parent, capped at 35 days per parent across all children, and 30 per child for single parents, capped at 70. The payment is 90 percent of the net pay you lose and your employer owes you unpaid release from work for those days. From 1 January 2027 the figures fall back to 10 and 20 working days per child, capped at 25 and 50, unless the law is extended again.

items.q: What happens if I fall ill during my annual leave?
items.a: Days of incapacity proved by a medical certificate are not counted against your annual leave, so you get them back. That only works with a certificate, which is why it is worth seeing a doctor even for a short spell during a holiday. Being ill is not in itself protection against dismissal in Germany, so do not assume a certificate changes anything about notice.
